comment: Declarative registry of every third-party asset. Nothing binary is committed:
`npm run assets:fetch` downloads into public/assets/, verifies the hash, and
regenerates CREDITS.md. `npm run assets:verify` runs in CI and fails on an
unlicensed entry, a missing attribution, or a hash mismatch.
sha256 null means the hash has not been recorded yet. Run
`npm run assets:fetch -- --record` on a machine that can reach the host and
the hash is written back here, pinning the file from then on.
EVERY asset here is optional. role 'flora' means a model that replaces one
species' procedural shape in src/config/flora.js; with none of them fetched
the valley is drawn entirely out of procedural geometry and is complete. See
rule 4 in CLAUDE.md — this is the rule the whole renderer is built around.
Two provenances. 'remote' entries are fetched and pinned automatically.
'local' entries CANNOT be fetched from the environment this project is built
in — quaternius.com, itch.io, poly.pizza, kenney.nl, ambientcg.com and
polyhaven.com are all blocked by its egress policy — so they name the pack,
the licence and the file they want, and wait for a human to supply it.
`npm run assets:link -- <folder>` matches a downloaded pack's GLBs onto them
by name; `npm run assets:fetch -- --record` then pins the hashes.
The art direction is Quaternius's Stylized Nature MegaKit, which is what the
local entries are for. Kenney's tree and cactus models are close enough, reachable,
and pinned as the remote fallback so a fresh clone still upgrades to real
models without a download page.
Every remote URL is pinned to a commit rather than a branch. A branch URL
would drift and fail its own recorded hash the next time upstream pushed.
